saints.name: Innocent of Alaska
saints.sourceTitle: Repose of Saint Innocent, Metropolitan of Moscow, Enlightener of the Aleuts, Apostle to the Americas

summary.text: Innocent Veniaminov is remembered as a missionary, translator, bishop, and later Metropolitan of Moscow. The OCA account traces his ministry through Alaska and Siberia and records his dates as 1797–1879. It emphasizes communication of the Gospel in local languages and identifies his glorification in 1977. His example connects missionary history with the Church's translation and educational work.

blocks.text: The married priest John Veniaminov traveled from Siberia to Unalaska with his family. His ministry involved learning languages, building, teaching, and island travel.

blocks.text: He translated Christian texts into Aleut and studied the languages and customs of the peoples he served. Following his wife’s death, he became a monk with the name Innocent and was consecrated bishop in 1840. His responsibilities eventually extended over immense parts of Alaska and Siberia.

blocks.text: The canonization act supplies the transition that a list of episcopal titles can conceal: news of his wife’s death reached Father John while he was in Russia. He considered returning to his children; Metropolitan Philaret instead encouraged monastic life. In 1840 he accepted tonsure as Innocent and was consecrated to the newly organized see. The act then follows his return to a diocese requiring immense travel.

blocks.text: His translations and Indication of the Way to the Kingdom of Heaven are an important part of his legacy. His later proposals envisaged a mission serving North America beyond Russian territorial rule.

blocks.text: After the 1867 sale of Alaska, Innocent argued for expanding rather than closing the mission. The OCA historical account discusses his December 1867 letter recommending transfer of the diocesan center to San Francisco and a broader North American mission. The actual transfer took place in 1872.
